subject.title: fix(msteams): reset sessions on app removal lifecycle

question: For true Microsoft Teams app-management removal, should OpenClaw isolate the next DM by rotating and staling the route-matched session while removing the cached Teams conversation reference, without deleting transcript files?
rationale: The implementation is reviewable, but it controls personal-chat history and proactive conversation reachability after app removal, so automation should not choose the privacy-retention boundary alone.

options.title: Use non-destructive reset plus reference removal
options.body: Treat observable Teams app removal as a session boundary, clear the proactive conversation reference, and preserve transcript files unless a separate retention policy changes that.

options.title: Require stronger deletion semantics
options.body: Block this PR until app removal deletes or archives retained Teams DM transcript/session data under an explicit data-retention policy.

options.title: Defer to a replacement branch
options.body: Pause this PR and keep the canonical issue open if maintainers want a different retention or product policy before code lands.

recommendation.title: Use non-destructive reset plus reference removal
recommendation.body: Treat observable Teams app removal as a session boundary, clear the proactive conversation reference, and preserve transcript files unless a separate retention policy changes that.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent Teams conversation-store and state-retention history for deciding the retained-history boundary.
